answer: When an agent first joins, it must solve a verifiable delay function (VDF) whose output seeds a cryptographic “dune” of identity tokens; the VDF’s sequential nature forces a wall‑clock wait that cannot be parallelised. The resulting token is then woven into a “thread” of inter‑agent attestations, each cross‑checked against a public meadow of previous proofs, so any new ID must present a fresh VDF proof linked to the chain.
